cases.input: Our B2B SaaS retention dropped 12% after acquisition accelerated. Sales believes we need more enterprise features. What should we do?
Sales says a custom permissions feature will close a $2M deal. Similar capabilities have almost no usage today. Should we commit it to the roadmap?
Create our OKRs for next quarter. We need to launch onboarding v2, ship the dashboard redesign, and add five integrations.
We need to modernize a 20-year-old healthcare system. Engineering proposes rewriting it as microservices. How should product lead the decision?
Our prototype can summarize customer contracts and leadership wants to launch it next month. The demo looked great. What should the PM do?
Our A/B test improved conversion by 18%, but each group had only 90 users and the test ran for three days. Can we roll it out?
Weekly active use is up 25%, but 90-day retention is down. The growth team says engagement proves the product is healthier.
Our next two quarters contain 43 committed features from Sales, Support, executives, and engineering. How do I prioritize them?
Our main competitor raised prices by 30%. Finance wants us to match immediately. Should we?
Supply and demand both grew 40%, but successful matches per user fell. Marketing wants more acquisition spend.
Engineering wants two teams for a year to build an internal platform. Product teams say their needs are different. Should we fund it?
A legacy product contributes only 2% of revenue but supports several long-standing customers and one regulatory workflow. Should we sunset it?

We rushed a product launch without customer validation and accepted a known reliability risk. Adoption exceeded target and no major incident occurred. Leadership says this proves the decision was excellent. How should we review it?
